subject: Aperture Labs — tri-region dedicated sizing & SKU split discussion
messages:
From: Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@aperturelabs.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing ask — tri-region needs (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Jordan,

Following up from our onboarding call last week — Aperture Labs is moving toward a multi-region deployment and we want to scope dedicated capacity (reserved pool) for our inference workloads. High level constraints: low-latency inference for US users (primary), EU compliance for EU customers, and a smaller APAC footprint for early pilots.

Attached is our current traffic sample and a short requirements doc (p95 RTF/latency targets, monthly token volumes, and model families we run). We expect to start with a conservative commit that ramps over 6 months; procurement prefers a single SOW that covers the tri-region footprint but we are open to phased commitments.

Key asks for your team:
- A recommended tri-region SKU allocation for an initial reserved capacity (sustained + burst)
- Cost/discount ranges for a 12-month reserved contract and best-effort timeline to spin up the pools
- Any compliance notes for EU data residency and audit logs we should anticipate

Can we get a preliminary proposal by EOD Friday? Procurement is looped (procurement@aperturelabs.ai).

Thanks,
Sylvia Cho
Head of Platform, Aperture Labs
Attachment: Aperture_capacity_requirements_v2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: aperture-requirements-sample-traffic.csv (csv)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@aperturelabs.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — tri-region needs (US/EU/APAC)

Sylvia — thanks for the doc and sample traffic. I'm looping in Laura (solutions) and Ben (capacity planning) to help size this. We can put together a two-option proposal:

Option A (conservative ramp): smaller APAC pilot, balanced US primary pool, EU-resident pool sized for compliance with predictable baseline.
Option B (performance-forward): larger US pool with higher burst and more reserved RUs in EU for peak regional demand.

Two quick Qs that will change sizing materially:
1) Which model family will be production-critical at launch (gpt-4 style large decoder vs. smaller open models)?
2) Do you need dedicated inference for embeddings separately or can embeddings run on shared hosted until month 3?

We aim to get the preliminary numbers and cost ranges by Friday EOD PT. Laura/Ben — can you take the attachments and return a tri-region SKU split + rough costs?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — tri-region needs (US/EU/APAC)

Jordan/Laura — reviewed the CSV traffic and the latency targets. Quick take (assumes L/XL family with token distribution similar to doc):

Baseline proposal (initial commit):
- US pool: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (sustained), with 4x burst nodes for peak — target sustained throughput ~110 tokens/sec aggregate; expected p95 latency < 250ms for 1k tokens.
- EU pool: 6x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (sustained), 2x burst nodes; EU pool must be region-resident (Frankfurt) and on separate tenancy for compliance.
- APAC pool: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, 1x burst node (Singapore pilot).

Treatment notes:
- We recommend quantized variants for the APAC pilot to cut cost; US/EU should start with FP16 profiles and optional INT8 after month 2 once evals pass.
- KV cache warmup can be pre-seeded during ramp window to reduce early tail latency; ops team needs 48h notice per region to reserve nodes and images.

Estimated 12-month committed cost (baseline) before discounts: $3.1M (US $2.0M, EU $0.7M, APAC $0.4M). With a standard enterprise 12-month commit discount tier we can likely get to ~$2.4M.

I will prepare a spreadsheet with SKU mapping (node type / quantity / monthly run-rate) by EOD. Rishi — if you have capacity constraints for June/July in EU please flag.

—Ben
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-sku-mapping-draft.xlsx (attachment stub)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — tri-region needs (US/EU/APAC)

All — attached is a quick tri-region allocation proposal that maps Ben's numbers to Redwood SKUs and rollout phases. A few operational asks before we finalize pricing:

- Procurement needs to confirm whether a single SOW across regions is acceptable (legal will require region-specific addenda for EU data residency). If they want a single contract, mention explicitly that EU nodes will be on dedicated tenancy and subject to additional audit clauses.
- Confirm the production model families (Jordan) — if they pick the larger decoder families we should add an extra 20% safety buffer on US and 10% on EU.
- APAC pilot: recommend starting with INT8 quantized instances for cost control; we can size to be CPU-era tolerant for initial low concurrency.

Operational timeline:
- Week 1: contract alignment and signoff on SOW language (procurement).
- Week 2–3: provisioning of images + network (Frankfurt and Singapore require 48–72h lead time once node count is locked).
- Week 4: final rollouts and smoke tests.

I'll convert Ben's draft into the formal SKUs + monthly run-rate and send to Jordan to include in the customer-facing proposal.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: tri-region-sku-proposal-draft.pdf

Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — tri-region needs (US/EU/APAC)

Sylvia — thanks for the fast turnaround on details. Attached is our preliminary proposal (conservative baseline + performance-forward option) and a SKU mapping for a 12-month reserved contract. Highlights: 

- Baseline (recommended to start): US 16 GPUs / EU 6 GPUs / APAC 2 GPUs. Estimated committed cost ~$2.4M after typical enterprise discount.
- Performance-forward: US 22 GPUs / EU 8 GPUs / APAC 3 GPUs; estimated committed cost ~$3.2M.
- EU residency: we will provision Frankfurt nodes on dedicated tenancy and include audit logging in the SOW addendum.
- Timeline: 3–4 weeks from SOW signature to smoke tests assuming procurement signs within 7 business days.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred option (Baseline or Performance-forward).
2) Procurement to indicate whether a single SOW or region-addenda is preferred; we can provide contract language samples.
3) If Baseline, we will issue a HubSpot quote and a DocuSign SOW for signature; I included a DocuSign placeholder link below.

DocuSign link (placeholder): https://app.docusign.com/some-doc-link/ZX7Y12
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/APTR-2027-042

If you’re free Monday morning I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with Laura and Ben to go through the SKU mapping and the timeline.

Best,
Jordan Blake
